name: clang-tidy

oneOf.$comment: DEPRECATED. clang-tidy versions 14.0.0 and below accept this array form.

Checks.description: Comma-separated list of globs with optional '-' prefix. Globs are processed in order of  appearance in the list. Globs without '-' prefix add checks with matching names to the set, globs with the '-' prefix remove checks with matching names from the set of enabled checks.

ExcludeHeaderFilterRegex.description: Regular expression matching the names of the headers to exclude diagnostics from. Diagnostics from the main file of each translation unit are always displayed. Must be used together with --header-filter. Can be used together with -line-filter.

ExtraArgs.description: Additional argument to append to the compiler command line

ExtraArgsBefore.description: Additional argument to prepend to the compiler command line

FormatStyle.description: Style for formatting code around applied fixes.

HeaderFileExtensions.description: File extensions to consider to determine if a given diagnostic is located in a header file.

HeaderFilterRegex.description: Regular expression matching the names of the headers to output diagnostics from. Diagnostics from the main file of each translation unit are always displayed. Can be used together with -line-filter.

ImplementationFileExtensions.description: File extensions to consider to determine if a given diagnostic is located in an implementation file.

InheritParentConfig.description: If this option is true in a config file, the configuration file in the parent directory (if any exists) will be taken and the current config file will be applied on top of the parent one.

SystemHeaders.description: Display the errors from system headers. This option overrides the 'SystemHeaders' option in .clang-tidy file, if any.

UseColor.description: Use colors in diagnostics. If not set, colors will be used if the terminal connected to standard output supports colors.

User.description: Specifies the name or e-mail of the user running clang-tidy. This option is used, for example, to place the correct user name in TODO() comments in the relevant checks.

description:
The current clang‑tidy configuration enables every check by default but explicitly disables the entire clang‑analyzer suite (Checks: “*,-clang-analyzer-*”). Specific options have been tuned: the modernize‑use‑auto check will only suggest auto when the type name is at least three characters long (modernize-use-auto.MinTypeNameLength = 3); identifier naming prefers camelCase for variables (readability‑identifier‑naming.VariableCase = camelCase); and the cppcoreguidelines‑pro‑type‑member‑init check is set to ignore arrays (cppcoreguidelines-pro-type-member-init.IgnoreArrays = true). Diagnostics from any header whose name ends with “_generated.h” are filtered out (ExcludeHeaderFilterRegex = .*_generated\.h), while all other headers are included (HeaderFilterRegex = .*). The tooling is instructed to prepend “-Iinclude” to the compiler command line and to add the flags “-std=c++20” and “-Wall” afterwards (ExtraArgsBefore = -Iinclude; ExtraArgs = [-std=c++20, -Wall]). Code fixes will be formatted according to the project’s .clang‑format file (FormatStyle = file), and header files with extensions .h, .hpp, and .hh are recognized as such, whereas implementation files are identified by the .cpp extension.

Inheritance from a parent configuration is disabled (InheritParentConfig = false), and diagnostics from system headers are shown (SystemHeaders = true). Colored output is enabled (UseColor = true), and any warning will be treated as an error (WarningsAsErrors = *). The configuration records the user as Jane Doe <jane.doe@example.com>.
